summary_html: Family agrees to a **voluntary service plan**—counseling, substance-use treatment, parenting classes—designed to correct conditions without court compulsion. Federal law prioritizes family preservation through prevention and support services.

- **SSA Title IV-B (42 U.S.C. §§ 620–629m)** — child-welfare services and family-preservation funding

key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed termination of the mother's rights and the foster parents' adoption, holding the record supported the neglect ground in section 211.447.5(2) despite years of offered services, and that consent to adoption was therefore not required under section 453.040.
key_cases.relevance: The Court treats the long record of voluntary and offered services — parent aide, therapy, drug testing, supervised visitation — as the measure of whether the parent corrected the conditions, which is exactly what a voluntary service plan is judged against.
key_cases.quote: For the reasons set out below, this Court finds the record supports termination on the ground of neglect under section 211.447.5(2).

key_cases.case_name: In the Interest of T.W.C. v. Children's Division of the Division of Social Services
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed termination of an incarcerated father's parental rights, holding that although incarceration alone is not a ground for termination under section 211.447.7(6), it does not excuse a parent from maintaining a continuing relationship through communication and visitation, and that additional services would not have permitted return within an ascertainable period.
key_cases.relevance: The case measures whether the services offered to the parent — including counseling — could have produced return of the children, which is the test a voluntary service plan must satisfy.
key_cases.quote: While incarceration alone shall not be grounds for termination of parental rights, section 211.447.7(6), it does not discharge a parent's obligation to provide the child with a continuing relationship

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed the appointment of third-party co-guardians over three children, holding that ample evidence supported the finding under section 475.030.4(2) that the parents were unwilling, unable or unfit to fulfill their duties as guardians.
key_cases.relevance: The mother's participation in and relapse from drug treatment is the record against which the court measured whether services had corrected the conditions.
key_cases.quote: The trial court's judgment found the children's parents (Mother and three separate fathers) unwilling, unable, or unfit to fulfill their duties as guardians under Section 475.030.4(2).

key_cases.holding: The Court reversed the termination of the mother's parental rights and remanded, holding that past acts support termination only when convincingly linked to predicted future harm, that findings supporting the earlier assumption of jurisdiction must be updated to describe the parent's condition at the time of the termination hearing, and that the trial court's findings here were insufficient on every ground relied on.
key_cases.relevance: The Court treats the mother's full compliance with the voluntary parenting plan as affirmative evidence against termination, showing what a service plan is worth when the parent performs it.
key_cases.quote: To that end, a trial court cannot support a termination by merely incorporating earlier findings supporting its assumption of jurisdiction or some other earlier disposition.
